overall_summary: Space-themed videos featuring extreme, mind-bending physical paradoxes or sensory contrasts (like burning ice or smelling like steak) are the clear drivers of high engagement and views. Meanwhile, repetitive psychology and brain-related facts struggle to capture attention, indicating audience fatigue or weak visual hooks in that niche.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' reached 1,053 views (the highest in the set), followed by 'The Largest Ocean in Space' (460 views) and 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like?' (368 views).
winning_patterns.action: Double down on astronomical anomalies that present extreme physical contrasts (e.g., burning ice, metal rain, diamond oceans) and use sensory-rich hooks.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees?' (302 views) and 'This Animal Literally Dies Every Winter!' (179 views) performed well above the channel average.
winning_patterns.action: Create content around shocking biological survival mechanisms or historical timelines of animals that defy common sense.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' got only 38 views, and 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' struggled with 54 and 5 views across duplicate uploads.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from generic brain/psychology facts unless they can be tied to a highly unusual, specific historical mystery or scientific anomaly.

weak_patterns.evidence: Uploading the exact same video title and concept within days (e.g., 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' or 'Why Space Is Completely Silent') consistently yields lower or split performance.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid immediate re-uploading of underperforming concepts; instead, re-edit the hook and change the title entirely before trying again.

next_video.reason: Matches the highly successful 16-second format and aligns with the posting time of the top-performing 'Burning Ice' video (12:44 PM UTC).
